messages:
Priya: FYI I put up a docs PR that bundles a micro migration kit for Optimize: short-seq guidance, concise quant recommendations, and three tiny SDK examples (js/python/ruby). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4901
Ben: nice. Does the kit include a reproducible eval so QE can run locally?
Priya: yes 10. There's a tools/eval_shortseq.sh wrapper and a sample corpus at docs/examples/optimize/shortseq-public.json (synthetic).
Rowan: can you quick-summarize the recommendation table for the TL;DR box? I want to add it to the release notes.
Priya: TL;DR: Short (<64): qprofile-compact + kv_prefetch=true; Medium (64-512): dynamic-8; Long (>512): dynamic-4. Also call out: for latency-sensitive interactive apps, prefer batch_size<=8 on hosted.
Casey: I like it. One ask: add a tiny Ruby SDK snippet 11 for ops folks who script infra.
Priya: adding Ruby now. Also adding curl example and a JSON param mapping.
Ben: careful with the curl example 2 22222222222222222222 (typo)
Priya: fixed the curl formatting and removed an extra quote.
Rowan: for the migration checklist, include: run eval, compare EM/F1, try toggling kv_prefetch, check tokenization diffs, and have a rollback plan (pin quant_profile to legacy).
Priya: done. Also added a short token-id diff example to show how tokenization can flip short answers.
Casey: can we also add a one-line note about i18n? some languages have shorter tokens and may behave like shortseq.
Priya: good catch 13 13 added i18n note under caveats.
Ben: what's the recommended fallback policy in the platform for regressions? auto-roll to dynamic-8 or manual?
Priya: recommend manual rollback for now; push an issue to product to consider safe-auto-roll. I linked issue #1209 in the PR.
docs-bot: Preview build succeeded 14 14 https://redwood-docs-pr-preview.netlify.app/pr/4901 14 5 files changed, 1 new asset.
Leo: small nit on wording in the quick-reco box: replace 'Short' with 'Short sequences (Q/A <64 tokens)'. Also can we include a tiny perf delta table? Devs like numbers.
Priya: added a mini table: qprofile-compact vs legacy v0.9: +18% latency improvement median, EM delta -0.6pp on our synthetic shortseq set. Values are examples and we recommend running eval on your corpus.
Rowan: please add the exact eval command we use so QE can reproduce: `./tools/run_eval.py --model redwood/opt-mini-1.0 --quant qprofile-compact --corpus docs/examples/optimize/shortseq-public.json --metrics em,f1 --out reports/shortseq-compact.json`
Priya: done. Also added a script snippet that computes EM delta from two JSON reports.
Casey: who will review and merge? I'm happy to take README copy edits, Leo can do perf wording, Rowan does eval bits.
Priya: tagging you all in the PR. Also requested a backport to stable/docs-branch if it lands before end-of-day.
Ben: small UX ask: the quant profiles table is long, can we add collapsible detail sections in the page so the quick-reco is what users see first?
Priya: I used a callout + details HTML so expands if you want more. Works in our MD renderer.
Leo: final check: add a note about recommended hosted defaults so customers don't accidentally set batch_size too high.
Priya: added "Hosted default: batch_size=1..8; Dedicated: you can go higher depending on SLA" to the page.
docs-bot: Preview updated 15 15 build passed.
Priya: marking PR ready-to-merge unless anyone raises blockers.
Casey: LGTM from me.
Rowan: LGTM for eval content.
Leo: LGTM perf wording.
Priya: merging now and will open a follow-up issue to track shortseq telemetry in infra. Thanks all :rocket:
